model.title: National Plan for Epilepsy Act
model.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-MO)

summary.text: The bill would require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to review federal programs, research, and strategic plans related to epilepsy, including research, prevention, early identification, diagnosis, and treatment, and to recommend updates to Congress. The review would cover findings from evidence-based research, gaps in knowledge, disparities among people with epilepsy, coordination between federal programs, and ways to improve collaboration, early diagnosis, care, surveillance, and support for new treatments. The Secretary would regularly seek input from other federal agencies, patient advocates, and outside experts. Within two years of enactment, the Secretary would report the findings to the Senate health committee and the House energy and commerce committee, including steps taken to gather stakeholder input, recommendations for better coordination, and any changes to programs or barriers to implementing them.
